title: daphne kurdica
intro: Daphne kurdica, commonly known as Kurdish spurge, is a plant species that belongs to the family Thymelaeaceae. It has been traditionally used in folk medicine to treat various health issues, including fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions, due to its reported health benefits such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Daphne kurdica are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, that exhibit analgesic, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities. Furthermore, the plant's bioactive constituents, particularly its flavonoids and phenolic acids, have been shown to possess anti-cancer and anti-diabetic properties, making it a subject of interest in modern pharmacology.
